title: Sales enablement: Positioning, competitive briefs, pricing guidance, pitch deck outline, case studies, and security FAQ
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

This is the canonical sales enablement reference for Redwood Inference sales and solutions teams covering: positioning & messaging, short competitive briefs, a recommended pitch-deck outline, pricing guidance and negotiation levers, two short case studies for field use, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this doc as the single source for standard responses, slide text, and deal-level guidance.

Quick summary (elevator pitches)
- For product/engineering buyers: "Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLM-powered features predictable, cost-efficient, and production-ready across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- For security/compliance buyers: "We provide flexible private deployment options, strong encryption and audit logging, and enterprise SLAs so you can run LLM inference with enterprise controls and provable isolation."
- For platform / infra buyers: "We optimize throughput and unit economics with GPU-aware runtime, automatic caching/batching, and model-quantization recommendations so inference is efficient at scale."

Target personas and priority use cases
- ML Engineer / Infra Lead: reducing inference costs and keeping latency predictable. Typical objections: "We already self-host; why move?" Key messages: operational burden, tooling, and observability are solved; show cost/latency comparisons.
- Product Engineer / PM: time-to-market and feature velocity. Use messaging focused on SDKs, quickstarts, and model catalog.
- Security / Compliance: needs isolation, auditability, and data residency. Lead with Private deployment, KMS/HSM, SOC2 evidence.
- Platform / SRE: throughput and SLOs. Emphasize autoscaling, burst capacity, and routing policies.

Core positioning pillars (4):
1) Production-first performance: low-latency, GPU-optimized runtime with prefix/KV-cache and batching to meet strict SLOs.
2) Unified experience: single API and deployment model across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Buy once, choose where it runs.
3) Cost-aware controls: clear levers (batching, quantization, routing) and tooling to optimize unit costs without sacrificing quality.
4) Enterprise readiness: SLA-backed Dedicated, private deployments, audit logs, and security integrations.

Value props by product line (one-liners)
- Hosted API: fastest time-to-value for prototypes and production with pay-as-you-go and built-in observability.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity with predictable throughput and priority access to optimized models.
- Private: VPC/on-premise deployments for regulated or air-gapped workloads with full auditability.
- Console & Optimize: per-route cost/latency breakdowns, rollout automation, and model suggestions to cut unit cost.

Competitive brief (one-paragraph comparisons and battlecard bullets)
- OpenAI / API-first competitors: Strengths: widely adopted, large model ecosystem. Weaknesses: limited private deployment options, fewer dedicated reserved capacity controls, less granular routing for cost trade-offs. Redwood win themes: unified deployments, private options, cost controls and observability.
- Anthropic / Claude-style providers: Strengths: strong safety research and model flavors. Weaknesses: cadence and deployment flexibility. Redwood win themes: production tooling, deployment modes, and cost/latency controls for scale.
- Cloud-managed endpoints (AWS Bedrock / GCP Vertex AI): Strengths: cloud-native integrations and enterprise contracts. Weaknesses: vendor lock-in, variability in latency/cost per model. Redwood win themes: model-vendor neutrality, consistent API and routing policies across clouds, and specialized runtime optimizations for inference efficiency.
- Self-hosted / OSS runtimes: Strengths: cost control and deep customization. Weaknesses: maintenance burden and lack of enterprise observability. Redwood win themes: operational savings (people + infra), SLO-backed services, and built-in rollout/rollback and fallbacks.

Short competitive matrix (use in one-slide or battlecard)
- Columns: Feature | Redwood | OpenAI | Cloud Endpoints | Self-hosted
- Example rows (present as bullet-style in slide):
  - Deployment modes: Hosted / Dedicated / Private -> Redwood: yes; OpenAI: hosted; Cloud: hosted/dedicated-ish; Self-hosted: yes (ops).
  - Private networking (VPC/on-prem): Redwood: strong; OpenAI: limited; Cloud: vendor-specific; Self-hosted: yes.
  - Observability & cost breakdown: Redwood: token-level, per-route; OpenAI: limited; Cloud: variable; Self-hosted: custom.
  - SLA and reserved capacity: Redwood: Dedicated w/ SLA; OpenAI: enterprise add-ons; Cloud: depends; Self-hosted: N/A.
  - Runtime optimizations for cost: Redwood: automatic batching, KV cache, quantization suggestions; others: limited or require ops.

Suggested pitch-deck outline (10–12 slides)
1) Title slide: logo, tagline, one-liner value prop.
2) Problem: cost/latency/operational risk when taking LLMs to production.
3) Why now: model proliferation + complexity of serving at scale.
4) Redwood solution: unified runtime and deployment modes (diagram).
5) How it works (high level): runtime, kernel selection, caching, routing.
6) Developer experience: API/SDKs, quickstarts, and example code snippet.
7) Performance & cost: p50/p95 latencies, cost per 1k tokens vs alternatives (anonymized).
8) Security & compliance: private deployment, audit logs, KMS/HSM, SOC2.
9) Pricing and commercialization (see guidance below).
10) Customer proof points: two short case studies.
11) Roadmap & enterprise services: Dedicated, SLA, migration support.
12) Call to action: pilot proposal and next steps.

Pricing guidance and negotiation levers (field guidance, not public website copy)
- Hosted API (typical ranges):
  - Text generation: $0.02–$0.08 per 1,000 input+output tokens depending on model family and SLA.
  - Embeddings: $0.0005–$0.003 per embedding (model-dependent).
  - Volume discounts: tiered discounts starting at committed $/month thresholds (discuss with sales ops).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity):
  - Monthly reserved pools priced by GPU type and committed throughput. Example: $12k–$30k per GPU-month depending on instance class and negotiated support SLA.
  - Multiyear discounts and ramp schedules available for enterprise deals.
- Private deployment / Enterprise license:
  - Platform license + support: typical starting point $50k/year platform fee for small campus deployments, scalable to $250k+/year for large customers with premium support and on-prem packaging.
  - Professional services: migration, custom integration, and compliance mapping charged separately.

Negotiation levers for ACV expansion
- Bundling: combine Dedicated commit + extended observability retention for a single price.
- Commitment term: longer terms enable deeper discounts.
- Performance tiers: offer burstable capacity vs dedicated baseline.
- Data residency & compliance add-ons: priced per-region or per-audit evidence package.

Deal sizing and play examples
- SMB proof-of-concept: Hosted API + 6 months of free credits + 1 small eval rollout.
- Mid-market: Dedicated 3–6 GPU-month commit + 3-month pilot + rollout support.
- Enterprise: Private deployment + platform license + 12–24 month support agreement + professional services.

Sales objection handling (top 10)
1) "We can self-host cheaper" -> Response: Total cost of ownership includes ops time, reliability risk, and slower feature velocity. Provide cost model comparison using customer inputs; highlight observability and fallbacks.
2) "We need on-prem / air-gapped" -> Response: Offer Private deployment / on-prem packaging and HSM/KMS integrations; reference customer A case study.
3) "We’re concerned about data leakage" -> Response: Explain per-request isolation, optional customer-managed keys, and audit logging.
4) "Latency is inconsistent in cloud" -> Response: Describe Dedicated pools, region pinning, and p95 latency targets with examples.
5) "We use multiple clouds" -> Response: Redwood is model- and cloud-neutral with routing policies to optimize cost and latency.

Case studies (2 short vignettes for slides / sales narratives)
- FinTech customer (mid-market): Problem: unpredictable inference cost and frequent timeouts during peak trading hours. Solution: Moved to Redwood Dedicated with autoscaling and workstation-grade GPUs for critical routes. Result: 45% reduction in per-token cost for production workflows, p95 latency improved from 840ms to 180ms, and one-month rollback capability standardized across releases.
- SaaS customer (AI-native content platform): Problem: embedding generation pipeline had high variance and lacked observability. Solution: Adopted Hosted API + Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching + quantization profile). Result: embedding cost reduced by 60% and throughput increased 3x during busy windows; platform released a new feature 6 weeks faster.

Security FAQ for prospects (concise Q&A for field use and customer-facing handouts)
Q: Where is customer data stored?
A: By default hosted API metadata and logs are stored in our multi-region cloud with region selection options. For regulated customers we provide Private deployments and region-specific hosting to meet data residency requirements.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
A: Yes. We support integration with customer KMS providers and HSM-backed key management for Private deployments and select Dedicated contracts.

Q: How do you handle audit logging and access controls?
A: Redwood Console provides tenant-level audit logs, API-level access traces, and role-based access control (RBAC). Logs can be exported to the customer’s SIEM.

Q: What compliance certifications do you have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II for our control plane. For Private/on-prem deployments we provide artifacts and support customer SOC2/ISO mapping exercises; additional compliance work is scoped per-customer.

Q: Can Redwood run in an air-gapped environment?
A: Yes. We offer an on-prem packaging option that supports air-gapped deployments; contact solutions engineering for the checklist and lead times.

Q: How do you prevent model/data leakage between tenants?
A: We enforce tenant isolation at the serving layer, dedicated caches per-tenant, and provide model variant pinning and routing policies. Private deployments can be deployed on customer-controlled networks for stronger isolation.

Q: Do you provide SLA and incident response?
A: Dedicated customers can receive SLA-backed uptime and latency targets (example: 99.9% platform availability for reserved pools). Our incident response includes a designated escalation path and on-call rotations for enterprise contracts.

Q: How are security fixes and runtime updates handled?
A: Hosted platform updates are managed by Redwood and scheduled with advance notices for breaking changes. For Private deployments, we provide an upgrade and rollback playbook and can coordinate staged patching with customer windows.

Appendix / Helpful snippets for calls
- Quick technical snippet (JavaScript SDK):
  const res = await redwood.generate({ model: 'rwd-moderate-1', prompt: 'Summarize customer support tickets', max_tokens: 256 });
- Pilot checklist (one-page):
  1) Define success metrics (latency target, cost per 1k tokens, quality threshold)
  2) Choose deployment mode (Hosted evaluation / Dedicated pilot / Private POC)
  3) Provision test dataset and access controls
  4) Execute 2-week traffic replay and record p95 latency and token cost
  5) Share results and propose production roll plan
